newsitem.title: KUWAIT: U.N. arms envoy in Kuwait after Iraq talks.
newsitem.headline: U.N. arms envoy in Kuwait after Iraq talks.

text.p: U.N. envoy Richard Butler said on Friday he received a "positive response" during talks in Iraq on eliminating Baghdad's mass destruction weapons.

Butler said on arrival in Kuwait that he told Iraqi officials at the start of their talks this week "the time had come to have a new determination and a new spirit of cooperation on the task of getting rid of Iraq's weapons of mass destruction."

"On the whole, I thought we got a positive response, and we have worked out some plans for the future which if they bear fruit will be good," the official Kuwait News Agency quoted him as telling reporters.
The Australian envoy arrived in Kuwait on Friday for his first visit since assuming the responsibility of eliminating Iraq's mass destruction weapons.

Butler on July 1 replaced Sweden's Rolf Ekeus, who had led the United Nations Special Commission (UNSCOM) entrusted with overseeing the dismantling of Iraq's prohibited weapons since its inception soon after the 1991 Gulf War over Kuwait.

He said the plans address chemical and biological weapons and missile capabilities. "It is important that Iraq come forward and give more to the Commission on those baskets and what is in them so that we can verify that and hopefully empty them."
Ekeus had in the past complained of lack of funds, turning to Kuwait and its oil-rich Gulf Arab allies for financial assistance to enable the mission to continue its work.
